Valeriy Vyaltsev and seven co-authors work on multi-agent pathfinding, where many robots move at once through a shared space without collisions. Optimal solutions are NP-hard to compute, so practical solvers are decentralized and increasingly learned. Most learned agents act only on local observations, which limits how well neighbors can coordinate.

Their model, LC-MAPF, adds a learnable communication module so nearby agents exchange features over several rounds before acting. It works with both reinforcement learning and imitation learning training styles. Across varied test scenarios the system beat existing learning-based solvers on diverse measures. Notably, the communication did not hurt scalability, the usual price of talking agents, which keeps the method viable for large fleets.
arxiv-2605-07837:
Subrat Prasad Panda and two co-authors train hard oblique decision trees, the interpretable models favored in safety-critical tabular work like medical diagnosis, with ordinary gradient descent and no approximations. Differentiable tree methods usually soften the decision boundaries or fake the gradients with a straight-through estimator. Regression trees are especially awkward to optimize jointly.

Their representation, DTSemNet, recasts a hard oblique tree as a neural network that is semantically equivalent and invertible, so end-to-end training needs no softening at all. For regression they add an annealed top-k method that supplies accurate gradient signals where the straight-through estimator fails. On classification and regression benchmarks the trained trees beat state-of-the-art differentiable trees. The representation also serves as a programmatic policy in reinforcement learning.
arxiv-2605-07937:
Anmol Gulati and four co-authors ask not whether long-horizon AI agents should ask clarifying questions, but when. Agents running workflows of hundreds of steps can ruin a task with one wrong early assumption. Yet no prior work measured how the value of a clarification changes over the course of execution.

Their forced-injection framework delivers ground-truth clarifications at controlled points, across four kinds of missing information, three benchmarks, and several frontier models, in thousands of runs. Timing profiles differed sharply by information type: goal clarification lost nearly all value after the first tenth of execution, while input clarification stayed useful to about halfway. Asking after mid-trajectory was worse than never asking. A study of unscripted sessions found no frontier model asks inside the optimal window.
arxiv-2605-08037:
Ning Liu, Chuanneng Sun, Kristina Klinkner, and Shervin Malmasi improve how language models learn from human preferences. The usual method, Direct Preference Optimization, trains on pairs of answers. In practice, one prompt often yields many sampled answers, and reducing them to pairs wastes ranking structure and can add conflicting signals.

Their method, GraphDPO, builds a directed graph from the full ranking of answers for each prompt. A graph-based objective follows dominance links between answers and recovers plain pairwise training as a special case. Ties and incomparable answers are handled directly, so training uses the whole preference structure instead of scattered pairs.
arxiv-2605-08337:
Zachary Bogorad and Roni Harnik prove that entanglement caps how strongly a detector can amplify a signal coherently. Coherent enhancement boosts sensitivity across many detector designs, but preparing the needed quantum states is hard, and the authors show the difficulty is fundamental rather than technical.

Their bounds tie the scaling of coherent effects with system size to the single-mode entanglement entropy of the detector state, interpolating smoothly between incoherent and fully coherent behavior. The results apply to parameter estimation and to scattering alike. Read one way, they bound quantum Fisher information and hence precision through the Cramér-Rao limit; read another, they tell detector builders exactly what more entanglement would buy.
arxiv-2605-08437:
Ramon Pires and colleagues benchmark whether language models can judge, not just advocate. Legal AI tests usually ask for arguments or drafted documents, yet a legal system also needs decision makers who weigh rival claims, apply doctrine to facts, and write reasoned rulings.

Magis-Bench draws seventy-four questions from recent Brazilian competitive examinations for judicial posts, including multi-turn discursive questions and practical exercises requiring complete civil and criminal sentences. Twenty-three leading models were graded by four independent frontier models acting as judges, and the evaluators agreed strongly with each other. The benchmark gives courts and researchers a way to test judicial writing rather than advocacy alone.
arxiv-2605-08537:
Jacob Lee, Alexandra Le Reste, Claudia Scarlata, and Kameswara Mantha Bharadwaj study how star formation changes as galaxies merge. Their work uses visual labels from Cosmic Disco, a Zooniverse citizen science project about galaxy collisions. The sample holds close to five thousand merger candidates drawn from a large sky survey, most of them confirmed as mergers by volunteers.

Star formation rises only weakly as mergers advance, though the link is firmly real despite wide scatter. Late stages form stars faster than early ones, matching earlier work. Readers learn that trained volunteers can sort merger stages well enough to trace slow change across thousands of systems.
arxiv-2605-08637:
Yuming Zhang, Congyuan Duan, Dong Xia, Doudou Zhou, and Tianxi Cai align patient record codes across hospitals that label the same condition differently. Pooling records from many institutions strengthens medical models, but local codes are granular and unmatched, splitting one concept into many fragments. Their SMILE method treats shared concept summaries as privacy safe embeddings and uses sparse known links as weak guidance.

Same meaning codes are modeled as clusters on a sphere, yielding one unified picture per clinical concept. The estimator comes with error bounds and reliable cluster recovery, and tests on simulations plus real multi hospital data show cleaner alignment. Health data research gains a principled way to merge records without sharing raw data.
arxiv-2605-08837:
Odysseas Chlapanis and two coauthors ask how models ground vague words like justice or theory. For folks, such sense grows from lived acts, felt states, and shared life. No one thing can be pointed at. The team reruns famed trait list tests from mind science. They run them on twenty one top and open models. Models lean too hard on word links. They list too few traits tied to felt or inner states.

No model comes near the pact rate folks reach with each other. In a split task, models rate ground types well when asked in a straight way. That skill grows with size. Probes find inner marks for sense and social ground. The gap is in use, not in what is known.
arxiv-2605-09037:
Nicholas Jannsen and five co-authors ask whether ESA's Plato space mission, built to hunt planets, could also spot pairs of supermassive black holes orbiting each other. A few hundred candidate pairs have been claimed from surveys of active galaxies, but only a handful still hold up.

The team builds a catalog of more than twelve thousand bright quasars in Plato's planned fields, drawn from Gaia data. Using a camera simulator, they make mock light curves and test whether Plato could detect the flares such pairs produce when one black hole lenses the other. Their answer is yes for the brightest cases, which could confirm or rule out the best known candidate.
arxiv-2605-09237:
Russon and three colleagues speed up qubit mapping and routing, a major snag in quantum compilation. The problem bites hardest for trapped ion systems, where interactions demand ions be shuttled under strict movement, congestion, and trap limits. Their framework centres on a position graph, a unified picture of routing constraints, movement paths, and runnable spots that lets mappers work directly on shuttling hardware.

On that graph they speed up SABRE, a two way heuristic search, with relative move scoring that caches repeated move scores, and memoized fixes for repeated congestion. The optimisation removes redundant work without changing any routing or shuttling decision. The result is a practical route to scalable mapping and routing on trapped ion systems and across varied quantum hardware. Source code and data are promised on acceptance. The work pairs an architecture aware picture with cached heuristic scores, cutting wasted work where search repeats itself.
arxiv-2605-09337:
Paul and five colleagues propose FAR-SIGN, a method for learning that resists adversaries in parameter-server-worker systems. It updates along carefully designed directions using only signs, and a two-timescale mechanism offsets the bias that sign updates introduce. The method admits both first-order and zeroth-order versions and runs fully asynchronously, with no private reference dataset needed at the server.

The authors prove convergence to stationary points with probability one for smooth, nonconvex objectives. They also prove a near-optimal rate for first-order use and the standard rate for zeroth-order use, with iteration count driving both. Experiments on MNIST show FAR-SIGN beating robust aggregation methods on both accuracy and wall-clock time.
arxiv-2605-09437:
Hernandez Gomez and Russo study two numbers attached to a projective variety: its tangent degree and the degree of its tangent variety. The tangent degree counts how many tangent spaces at smooth points run through a typical point of the tangent variety, when that count is positive and finite. It is zero when the tangent variety is too small. The paper sets out general properties of both numbers, extending facts long known for plane curves to higher dimensions.

Among the results, the tangent degree can never be one when the ambient dimension is twice the variety dimension. When the tangent variety differs from the secant variety, its degree obeys a linear lower bound in terms of codimension. The authors then classify cases where those bounds are met, in small dimension or under smoothness, and classify varieties with tangent degree above one in small dimension.
arxiv-2605-09737:
Li proposed a structural fix for a basic weakness in large language models: system prompts and user text get equal treatment inside the model. That equal footing lets hostile user input overwrite safety rules, a prompt injection, and lets rules fade over long chats. CALYREX, short for Cross-Attention LaYeR EXtended transformers, routes system-prompt attention through dedicated cross-attention layers that anchor the rules apart from user content.

A placement test on a 1.5-billion-parameter backbone found the final eighth of layers optimal, matching where constraint behavior naturally concentrates. At 8-billion scale, CALYREX gained 7.4 percent on instruction-following and 16.3 percent on multi-turn adherence, while cutting many-shot jailbreak success by 13 percent. The edge widened with scale, suggesting bigger models use the dedicated routing best.
arxiv-2605-09937:
Blondin and five colleagues studied population protocols over ordered agents, extending a distributed model in which anonymous agents interact in random pairs and update states by fixed rules. Computation means settling to a consensus output. In practice, agents often carry unique IDs and compare them first. The paper therefore models agents as ordered, with interactions allowed only when the ID pair meets some condition.

The main result concerns the immediate-observation fragment IO-PP[<], where only one agent changes state per interaction and pairs must respect order. It recognizes exactly the unambiguous star-free languages, also described by two-variable first-order logic and two-way deterministic partially-ordered automata. A matching logic and automaton fit PP[<]. If the successor predicate joins a set of NSPACE(n) predicates, then IO-PP, PP, and NSPACE(n) coincide. The paper also asks whether a protocol always stabilizes.
arxiv-2605-10037:
Mei and Tang study exponential steadying, by output feedback, of a chained system joining an ordinary differential equation with a wave partial equation under boundary control. Four types of boundary link are covered. With no disturbances, a new transformation folds the wave equation's boundary control input into the ordinary subpart.

From that transformation the authors design a state feedback controller giving exponential steadiness to both parts. When internal unknowns and outside disturbances matching the control structure appear, a disturbance estimator is built, feeding a Luenberger-type observer that rejects upsets and steadies the whole system through watcher-based control. Boundedness of the entire closed loop is also proved rigorously.
arxiv-2605-10137:
Tan and five colleagues adapt prior-data fitted networks for Thompson sampling in contextual bandits, choice problems behind recommendation and adaptive trials. Thompson sampling draws a reward function from a Bayesian posterior each round and acts greedily under that draw. Prior-data fitted networks like TabPFN and TabICL approximate posterior predictive distributions in one forward pass.

The catch: these networks predict noisy future rewards, while Thompson sampling needs uncertainty over the latent mean reward. PFN-TS converts posterior predictives into mean-reward samples through a subsampled predictive central limit theorem. Variance is estimated from a geometric grid of prefixes rather than the full predictive sequence, and cached representations are reused across rounds. The paper proves consistency of the variance estimator and a Bayesian regret bound. PFN-TS earns the top average rank across nonlinear synthetic and OpenML benchmarks, plus the highest policy value in an offline health test.
arxiv-2605-10237:
Elisabetta Cornacchia, Dan Mikulincer, and Elchanan Mossel ask whether the order of training data can make a hard learning problem easy. Boolean k-juntas are functions that depend on only k of d inputs, a classic sparse-learning test case. Under independent uniform samples, gradient methods face strong barriers. Their 2026 paper shows that temporal correlation changes the picture.

When samples come from a lazy random walk on the hypercube, consecutive examples are correlated rather than independent. A two-layer ReLU network trained with stylized stochastic gradient descent and a temporal-difference loss, comparing target and predicted changes across consecutive samples, exploits that structure. For every fixed k, sample complexity becomes essentially linear in the ambient dimension d. By contrast, large-batch gradient methods with standard convex pointwise losses gain no such advantage from the correlations.
arxiv-2605-10437:
Yeonseok Lee brings formal proof to CNC machining safety, where a wrong tool path can crash a machine. Old verification relies on geometric simulation and swept-volume analysis. Those methods catch obvious G-code errors but cannot give symbolic proofs of safety. They also demand repeat retesting when specs change. His 2026 paper treats the physical CNC workspace as a Spatial Heap, with occupancy as a managed logical resource.

A Parser-Prover Handshake decouples machine kinematics from formal logic. It maps tool trajectories and safety buffers into a discrete spatial model before evaluation. Separation Logic then verifies safety via formal triples. Physical collisions become logical Spatial Data Races, detected when the separating conjunction fails to establish disjointness. Concurrent Separation Logic extends the method to collaborative settings, verifying hand-offs as ownership transfers. The framework scales to multi-axis setups such as 5-axis Table-Table by treating the workpiece as mutable.
arxiv-2605-10737:
Francisco J. G. de Oliveira, Zahra Sharif Khodaei, and Oliver R. H. Buxton present a lab test of wake-blade link in a model wind turbine, with a focus on tip-speed ratio under varied free-stream turbulence. Wake speed measures, taken at the same time as spread-out blade strain measures with Rayleigh backscattering fibre-optic sensing, allow direct time-matched study of fluid-structure link across the blade span.

Blade strain moves are ruled most by tip-speed ratio, which shifts size, order, and time and tone shape, while turbulence mostly tweaks these replies. Cycle-mean cross-correlation and cross-power tone studies show wake-driven replies bunched in shear bands and set round spin-matched tones, peaking at mid downstream spots. A steady negative-lag peak shows blade strain wobbles precede downstream wake speed wobbles, hinting at a causal blade-led mark on the wake.
arxiv-2605-11037:
Zheng Xing and eight colleagues map indoor radio environments without any location labels, a task that normally demands costly site surveys with precise user positions. Existing label-saving methods still need partial annotations or inertial sensors, which face hardware limits, access restrictions, and drift.

Their physics-informed framework uses only channel state information under known access-point geometry and a known walkable domain. A Power-Angle-Delay Profile feature distance, built from MIMO-OFDM channel data, proxies small spatial displacements through local multipath continuity, letting the system recover latent coordinates of measurements. Indoor-positioning teams get radio maps without survey crews or inertial hardware.
arxiv-2605-11237:
Yongsen Tan and four co-authors introduce DeconDTN-Toolkit, a library for testing and boosting toughness to provenance shift. This shift, where the link between data source and label changes at rollout, remains poorly mapped and unfixed despite growing work on distribution shifts.

The team ties this shift, counterfactual invariance, and invariant learning together formally to get a learning objective for toughness. DeconDTN-Toolkit is a custom evaluation and fix-it suite that mimics such shifts at varying strengths while keeping the training protocol and infrastructure of existing benchmarks. It reveals the vulnerability of Empirical Risk Minimization under such shifts, introduces a robust out-of-sample performance indicator, and evaluates current algorithms fully. Users get both theory and hands-on tools for mapping confounding by source and easing it.
arxiv-2605-11437: Gourdji and six colleagues revisit the neutron-star merger GW170817 with a new fitting framework for radio interferometry data. Past inclination estimates lean on jet afterglow light curves, which depend on the uncertain jet opening angle. Fitting new hydrodynamical afterglow models across many jet geometries, they obtain a viewing angle near eighteen to twenty degrees at fixed distance. Fitting distance and Hubble constant directly gives a viewing angle near seventeen to nineteen degrees and a Hubble constant of 65 point 5, close to the early-Universe Planck value.
arxiv-2605-11537: Jyothish and three colleagues propose dynamic expert replication for fast mixture-of-experts inference. These models scale capacity without matching compute, but inference wastes GPU time as tokens wait on the same experts. Their method predicts which experts will overload and copies them for coming token batches. Copied experts run at once across layers, raising parallelism and cutting idle time. On Switch-base-128 and Switch-base-256 it reaches near-full GPU use and up to three times faster inference while keeping about 90 to 95 percent of baseline quality.
arxiv-2605-11737: El Aitouni and five others study laser-aided tunnel in tungsten WSe2 under a laser field. Within Floquet math, driving yields wave functions across three regions, with smooth joins at edges giving flow and bounce for current. The laser induces a rich Floquet side structure growing with drive strength, cutting flow, beating Klein tunnel. Wider lit regions enhance fermion play, causing retune and trapped states, while Floquet mixing reduces sent current. Light-matter play enables dynamic control of quantum transport for tunable filters and switches.
arxiv-2605-11837: Brotin Taraphdar and three colleagues simulate how build flaws affect a digital quadrupole mass filter driven by rectangular waves. Changing rod radius and position adds octupole field parts that warp the ideal field. Mass resolution and ion throughput fell in every case tested. Results also hinge on the pulsed waveform's starting state. That finding sets build limits for high-resolution digital mass filter design.
arxiv-2605-12137: Marco Anarmo and three colleagues present NPAP, an open-source Python tool that shrinks network maps. Built on NetworkX, it splits the job in two: grouping nodes into clusters, then shrinking the net under that grouping. Its strategy design lets users add their own grouping and shrinking rules without touching core code. NPAP now ships 13 grouping rules and two set shrink profiles, built first for power grids but open to any network map.
arxiv-2605-12537: Alpay and Basaran model strategic social choice with two profiles per state: a true profile for welfare comparisons and a submitted report profile that the rule actually uses. Coalition moves replace only the coalition's reports, and their relations obey a fixed composition law for combined coalitions. The paper proves soundness and completeness of the logic Hbp for the abstract Dev frame class, with a reverse-composition midpoint in the canonical proof. It then separates abstract Dev components from genuine report-coordinate products, and adds an audit layer for representation changes.
arxiv-2605-12737: Basu and Flores provide new examples of C-star-selfless groups and inclusions. They prove the commensurator group of a torsion-free hyperbolic group is C-star-selfless. Their approach shows the Gromov boundary of the group is a topologically free extreme boundary for its commensurator and its automorphism group. It is also one for other groups containing the group in an almost normal way. The boundary argument thus yields selflessness for a whole family of groups built around hyperbolic groups, extending the known examples of such groups and inclusions.
arxiv-2605-12937: Lagogiannis, Agnew, Arriaga and Das propose AuraMask, a pipeline for anti-facial-recognition filters that stay both effective and good-looking. Earlier subtle filters still clash with how users want to present themselves, so adoption stays low. AuraMask produces 40 filters mimicking popular one-click social-media filters, matching or beating prior methods against open-source recognisers. In a 630-person study, users accept them far more readily than prior filters.
arxiv-2605-13137: Gao and seven co-authors present LeanSearch v2, a two-mode retrieval system for global premise retrieval in Lean 4 theorem proving: finding the scattered library lemmas a whole proof needs. Standard mode pairs a hierarchy-informalised Mathlib corpus with an embedding-reranker pipeline, topping single-query retrieval without domain-specific fine-tuning. Reasoning mode iterates sketch-retrieve-reflect cycles over that substrate. On a 69-query benchmark of research-level theorems it recovers 46.1% of premise groups within 10 candidates, and in a fixed prover loop it reaches the highest proof success at 20%.
arxiv-2605-13737: Trung Nguyen Quang and five colleagues offer IMAVB, a curated 500-clip test set of long-form movies testing premise-sense conflict spotting in all-sense word models. Across eight open-source all-sense models and Gemini 3.1 Pro, hidden states well encode premise-sense clashes even when models almost never reject false claims. Models show two failure modes: under-refusal, answering tricky questions as if false claims were true. Over-refusal means saying no to standard questions too and losing grasp hits.
arxiv-2605-14137: Li and seven co-authors tackle flow-field reconstruction from sparse sensor readings in real settings. High-quality flow data clashes with practical limits on sensor deployment, and past deep learning methods lean on simplifications: two-dimensional domains, preset equations, idealized synthetic data and free sensor placement. The paper's directional transport-aware graph neural network encodes both flow direction and information transport. It also shows old sensor placement plans often land on suboptimal setups.
arxiv-2605-14437: Rojas-Bravo and colleagues, in a 2026 study, search Type Ia supernovae from Zwicky Transient Facility Data Release 2 for early-time flux excesses, clues to progenitor systems and explosion mechanisms. Coverage and quality rules yield 42 early-excess events and 110 no-excess events from 1,547 supernovae. Two-sample tests show the strongest differences in light-curve properties. Early-excess events show larger SALT2 stretch and r-band secondary-maximum flux, while colour differences are weak. Early-excess events favour bluer colours and lower stellar masses. The results link early excesses to diversity.
arxiv-2605-14837: Liu, Savaux and Farhang make affine frequency division multiplexing secure against eavesdroppers through phase function design. AFDM uses chirp subcarriers with two tunable parameters, one handling Doppler effects and the second open for physical layer security. The authors derive a design criterion showing brute-force demodulation cost hinges on the phase function's first derivative. A family of phase functions is introduced that raises this cost without bound and under control while keeping chirp structure, with security gains of several orders claimed.
arxiv-2605-14937: Jonathan Spieler, Angel Villar-Corrales, and Sven Behnke present Slot-MPC, a planner that reasons about scenes object by object. Vision encoders learn slot representations, one per object, and an action-conditioned model predicts how those objects move. At run time, model predictive control plans actions through the learned model, and gradients make that planning faster than sampling-based rivals. Simulated robot manipulation trials show gains in both task success and planning efficiency.
arxiv-2605-15137: Amy H. Knight and four others report a new possible pulsating ultraluminous X-ray source in Centaurus A, listed as 4XMM J132542.2-425943. Visible as a clear point source for about eight months in 2014, it later appeared faintly in 2017 and 2024 and otherwise stayed quiet. Its soft X-ray spectrum sets it apart from known pulsing sources, which usually show hard spectra. One 2014 observation shows coherent sinusoidal pulsations at 1.27 hertz, though the authors probe whether instrument randomization could mimic the signal.
arxiv-2605-15237: Abinand Nallathambi and four others present A3D, an agentic AI pipeline for end-to-end design of hardware accelerators. Accelerator design stays labor-heavy, needing workload insight, hardware design, micro-architecture, and EDA tool skill, so most tools cover only regular flows. A3D runs workload analysis, choke-point spotting, code rework for high-level synthesis, and micro-architecture generation. It also maps the speed-area tradeoff space to produce diverse accelerator designs.
arxiv-2605-15437: Fabio Andrijauskas, Derek Weitzel, and Frank Wuerthwein describe the operation and monitoring of the Open Science Data Federation, a global data-access network growing out of StashCache. The federation adds origins and caches, access methods, and monitoring and accounting mechanisms to the earlier project. It has become integral to United States national cyberinfrastructure, uniquely positioned to meet sharing requirements in recent NSF solicitations. Many collaborations and individual users pull data through it to research infrastructures and projects worldwide.
arxiv-2605-15537: Jing Wang, Shang Liu, Hangan Zhou, and Zhiyao Xie build RTL-BenchMT, an agent-based system that maintains benchmarks for automatic chip-design code generation. Existing benchmarks suffer from flawed cases and from models overfitting to them, both hard to fix by hand. Their framework automatically finds and revises flawed cases and detects and updates overfitted ones, producing a refined suite for release. The work aims to cut human maintenance costs for a fast-moving evaluation area.
arxiv-2605-15837: Naoyasu Kita, Hayato Miyazaki and Takuya Sato prove a large-data L2-decay estimate for attractive-dissipative nonlinear Schrödinger equations. The energy lacks a fixed sign when the real part of lambda is negative, blocking the uniform gradient bound. They add a multiple of the shrinking L2-norm to form an augmented energy, which adds a dissipative term and yields a uniform-in-time H1 bound. This extends the known decay rate across the sharp range 1 < p ≤ 1 + 2/d for arbitrary initial data, removing the last restriction in this case.
arxiv-2605-16037: Bauret Martínez and three colleagues adapt Fast and Relaxed Vector Fitting to aircraft vibration testing. The frequency-domain tool comes from electrical engineering and was little used for mechanical systems. Their three-stage method fits frequency responses, extracts system poles, and recovers modal parameters. It matched existing methods on a beam model and on ground vibration data from a BAE Hawk T1A jet.
arxiv-2605-16137: Luo and seven colleagues present STABLE, a dual system that generates simulation-ready tabletop scenes from task instructions. Language-model-only layouts often yield collisions or floating objects, since such models reason weakly in 3D space. STABLE pairs a semantic reasoner that drafts coarse layouts with a physics corrector that refines poses for physical plausibility. Alternating the two modules expands scenes from task-critical objects to background items, with far better physical validity than prior methods.
arxiv-2605-16237: Wang and four colleagues study Major League Baseball's seven-year experiment with the Automated Ball-Strike System as a lesson in technological rule enforcement. The strike zone looks clearly defined in the rulebook, yet automating ball-strike calls took seven years of design decisions. Ground truth proves contested in practice, blending rulebook definition with umpires' enforcement habits, and implementation must balance many stakeholder values. The authors argue evaluation should focus on how such systems are experienced in practice, not just on rule-to-code distance.
arxiv-2605-16437: Fan and five others propose a one-hot coding unsourced random access system for message authentication without breaking that principle. Unsourced random access lacks device IDs, so decoded messages cannot be linked to devices, letting forged ones pass. Distinct messages map onto orthogonal channel uses via a one-hot common code set. The channel structure enables radio-frequency fingerprint identification to verify signals from hardware flaws. Per-user error and spoofing odds are derived, and results show secure sending in ultra-short-payload IoT settings.
arxiv-2605-16737: Sural and Rajkumar propose DriveSafer, a safety system for end-to-end self-driving planners that learns from failures. Generative planners still fail badly in safety-critical scenes, often by breaking physical limits and safety rules. DriveSafer steers planners toward safe behavior with safety limits in training and safety guidance at run time. On the NAVSIM test set, it cuts catastrophic failures against the DiffusionDrive model by 48%, with over 65% fewer drivable-area compliance failures.
arxiv-2605-16937: Zuo's team presents DEVIS-GRPO, the first online policy-gradient method for extreme-view video under camera control. Current methods handle small camera moves but fail on large ones, and past fixes needed costly paired video sets. Their sampler, ADEVIS, builds large camera moves by stacking small increments, which removes warm-starting on paired large-view videos and widens sample variety. A multi-level reward scoring consistency and quality picks samples for training. Tests on three datasets show clear gains, including about 22 percent better PSNR on Kubric-4D.
arxiv-2605-17137: Ahmed, Mostajabdaveh and Zhou move automated heuristic design from discrete program search into a continuous latent space. An encoder maps programs to embeddings, a surrogate predicts performance, and gradient ascent in a flow-regularized space yields new candidates that a frozen language model turns back into code. On routing, knapsack and packing problems the method matches leading evolutionary baselines.
arxiv-2605-17337: Wang and Yin determine the smallest equivariant embedding dimensions for orthogonal groups acting over real flag manifolds and unitary groups acting over complex ones. In both cases the minimum is attained at the isospectral model. The short paper settles the dimension question for these two families of group actions in one stroke.
arxiv-2605-17437: Li and colleagues propose the Semantic Mutation Score, an adequacy gauge for metamorphic testing in science programs. Classic mutation scores work on syntax trees and miss domain meaning. The new score closes that gap. It judges mutants by domain meaning rather than syntax alone, using five semantic operators: conservation erosion, operator substitution, hyperparameters, trajectory flips and structural injection. Tests on twelve programs find a medium effect, short of the preset large-effect threshold. Several operator classes, it also shows, are out of reach for default syntactic mutation.
arxiv-2605-17537: Xu and colleagues present ResDreamer, a hierarchical world model for visual reasoning in 3D open-world settings with hostile rivals. Each higher layer rebuilds the residuals of the layer below, abstracting world motion step by step and enriching latent codes. Higher-level residuals steer lower-level predictions, so the model scales with only slowly growing cross-layer talk. Trained purely self-supervised, it achieves leading sample and parameter efficiency in experiments.
arxiv-2605-17937: Zhensheng Wang and five colleagues introduce BacktestBench, the first large-scale benchmark for automated strategy backtesting. Backtesting judges trading strategies, but high barriers and poor scaling hamper automation. Built from over 6 million real market records, the benchmark holds 18,246 questions across metrics, ticker choice, strategy choice, and parameter checks. The team also offers AutoBacktest, a multi-agent baseline turning plain-language strategies into backtests that repeat. Tests on 23 language models highlight grounded proof and standard indicators as keys to results.
arxiv-2605-18137: Lijun Zhou's 2026 report joins two skills for self-driving cars: rebuilding a scene in three dimensions and making new video of it. One part builds compact 3D scenes from sparse queries spread across views and time, keeping frames in line with each other. The other part makes causal video in as few as four clean-up steps. Joined, the pair gives steadier video for closed-loop tests, fresh training data, and driver training.
arxiv-2605-18237: Julián Ferreiro-Vélez's 2026 paper tames counterdiabatic driving for the quantum Rabi model, working past the dispersive limit. Counterdiabatic control damps stray excitations during fast state prep, but trace-based variational designs break down for unbounded bosonic spaces, where cost functions diverge. The authors restrict the trace metric to displaced and low-energy subspaces, giving sound coefficients. The method yields two control terms linking the atom to the field's position and momentum parts, working from strong to deep-strong coupling, with Floquet implementation by parametric modulation.
arxiv-2605-18337: Ruggero Marino Lazzaroni's 2026 paper presents Infini-News, a toolkit and index for the Common Crawl news archive from August 2016 onward. Commercial archives charge prohibitive fees and licensing limits, while the open archive demands terabyte storage and heavy processing. The team extracts, cleans, and parses metadata for over 1.35 billion articles. Language detection from three classifiers and geographic attribution resolve a country for 83.4 percent of articles across 222 countries. Infini-gram indexes, built as suffix arrays, let researchers search the archive for text patterns in sub-second time.
arxiv-2605-18437: Yaorong Huang, Jingtao Luo, and Xuechao Wang present FedMAGS, a 2026 federated meta deep reinforcement learning system for shifting varied tasks in vehicular edge computing. Graph attention nets capture task links, a Seq2Seq policy makes structured shift choices, and federated meta-learning adapts across servers without sharing raw data. Tests show faster convergence, lower delay, better scale-up, and kept privacy with less communication load.
arxiv-2605-18837: Yuxuan Weng, Wenhan Luo and Qijia Shao tackle wearable health sensing when some sensor channels drop out. Rebuilding a whole missing signal can invent details the remaining sensors cannot support. Their VCR framework instead learns representations that survive gaps, splitting each modality into shared meaning and its own quirks. A missing-aware expert network adapts to whichever channels are present, and reconstructing only the shared part of a missing modality avoids hallucinations while beating strong baselines.
arxiv-2605-19137: Svetlana Orlova and two colleagues ask whether video models can be built by reusing a frozen image foundation model and training only a temporal module. Video foundation models usually need massive video pretraining, while image models already offer spatial representations. The authors freeze a pretrained image model as a spatial encoder and train only a recurrent temporal module for streaming video. Across several video understanding tasks, temporal performance emerges without large-scale video pretraining, suggesting future recurrent video models could be built this cheaper way.
arxiv-2605-19537: Pape, Evertz and Schönherr show the inference backend acts as a hidden hyperparameter in model evaluation. A survey finds 200 distinct engines, and an analysis of 35,000 publications finds the inference stack rarely reported. Holding weights, decoding settings and hardware fixed, they test five popular engines across open models and standard benchmarks. Backend choice alone moves scores by up to 16.6 percentage points and drives output disagreement. The divergence traces to prefix caching, CUDA graphs, custom kernels and engine logit defaults. The authors urge standardized reporting of inference stacks.
arxiv-2605-19637: Domelevo and team show the 3/2 power in the matrix-weighted Hilbert transform bound cannot be improved, even for the Poisson matrix A2 characteristic. The matrix A2 conjecture was recently disproved. Hilbert transform growth in matrix-weighted space is at most a constant multiple of the A2 characteristic to the 3/2 power. That bound was previously established and now proved sharp, ruling out linear growth. The natural question was whether the fatter Poisson characteristic softens the exponent. The authors prove it does not: the 3/2 power persists and cannot be improved.
arxiv-2605-19937: Marko sets out a way to turn time traces into frequency charts at any detail the user picks. The method tests a run of made up sine waves against the data and scores each by fit, then scales the scores into a sharp chart keeping size and phase. The chart can be turned back into the time trace, closing the loop.
arxiv-2605-20137: Useong Shin proposes a daily benchmark for post-crisis covered interest parity deviations. Deviations are observed, yet no canonical benchmark exists like standard asset-pricing factor models. On G10 plus KRW currency-tenor panels, three lagged variables deliver in-sample and out-of-sample performance: the NFCI, the nominal broad US dollar index, and the Treasury ten-year minus two-year slope. Cointegration, quarter-end and aggregation-difference checks suggest the benchmark captures a lasting background factor rather than quarter-end spikes at short maturities or spurious correlation.
arxiv-2605-20337: Julien Colin and three co-workers measure how people read foundation models. The framework tests localizability, guessing where a trait fires in new images, and semanticity, saying what the trait means. They ran six vision transformers, gathered over 15000 responses, and studied 13400 from 377. Foundation models read worse than size-matched supervised peers, with no trade-off: reading skill does not track task scores. Focal firing and broad class fit track it, and the two tests rank models the same, marking it as its trait of model quality.
arxiv-2605-20537: Robert Leaman, Rezarta Islamaj, and Zhiyong Lu ask what biomedical tests of name-spotting and concept-linking actually measure. They build a diagnostic framework that sorts corpus facts into five families, from size and label mix to train-test overlap. Applied to nine corpora for diseases, chemicals, and cell types, it shows corpora for the same task can differ sharply. They can demand different generalization and permit different reuse.
arxiv-2605-20737: Siqi Wei and six colleagues present LangTail, a language-guided framework for unsupervised 3D point-cloud segmentation. Purely visual grouping suffers long-tail ambiguity, where traits of rare classes get absorbed by big clusters and predictions skew badly. LangTail uses balanced world knowledge stored in language models to link language-derived meaning priors to underrepresented minor classes. Multi-level links between language priors and visual traits make up for visual grouping's bias toward big classes.
arxiv-2605-20937: Shuwang Chang and seven colleagues present the biggest statistical study to date of spike-type III burst pairs in solar radio emissions. Spike-like clusters appear atop the high-frequency onset of type III bursts, forming a distinct class. With high time-frequency detail data from the Chashan Broadband Solar radio spectrometer at meter wavelengths, they analyze 502 spike-type III pairs from 35 events recorded between November 2023 and October 2025. Spike clusters systematically precede their type III bursts by 0.5 to 3 seconds in time.
arxiv-2605-21137: Masaharu Tanabe sets new upper limits on the count of nonconstant holomorphic maps between compact Riemann surfaces, with the limit set by genus alone. Holomorphic maps are smooth complex maps that keep local angles intact. His bounds beat prior bounds. The proof looks at pullbacks of holomorphic differentials, using tools from the geometry of numbers and the theory of Jacobian varieties.
arxiv-2605-21537: Gokul Chandra Purnachandra Reddy and co-authors ask whether language models can self-review code modernization. Language-model agents increasingly migrate legacy code to modern stacks. The question is whether the same model spots silent behavior changes in its own output. They run one thousand nine hundred eighty modernization calls across eleven models on a sixty-snippet legacy-Python-2 corpus. Semantic-trap snippets drift in thirty-nine point seven percent of attempts, versus seven percent on benign controls.
arxiv-2605-21737: Xu studies Steinhaus random multiplicative functions, asking which sets of integers still show bell-shaped, complex normal fluctuations when their values are averaged. He proves that any set whose scaled average converges to that bell shape must have vanishing density relative to the whole range. The bound is sharp: for most sets at densities that approach one slowly, the bell shape survives once the average is rescaled by the leftover fraction.
arxiv-2605-21837: Marina Orio and coauthors present an unpublished NuSTAR observation of RS Oph's 2021 outburst, 9 days after maximum, plus a shock review. Gamma/X-ray fluxes from day 1 after the optical peak gave the first view of shocks in a symbiotic nova. The shock driving Cherenkov particle acceleration produced the thermal X-ray flux. The Fermi gamma flux after a day clashes with X-ray observations. An initial strong shock struck the red giant atmosphere, and shocks in the T CrB outburst may be less energetic than in RS Oph.
arxiv-2605-21937: Syed Tauhidun Nabi and co-authors evaluate four major IP geolocation providers against reference data from RIPE Atlas and UNICEF Giga across 175 countries. Mobile networks show median errors more than 10 times higher than fixed networks, and Global South geographies fare far worse than Europe. Both gaps trace to prefix granularity. Provider prefixes in mobile networks and the Global South are more likely coarser than BGP announcements, and about 70 percent of mobile prefixes span over 100 km. Coarser prefixes consistently yield the highest errors, for any provider, network type, or region.
arxiv-2605-22137: Soegeng and co-authors propose cross-lingual consensus for aligning multilingual cultural knowledge via self-consistency. Large language models perform unevenly across languages, and English prompting induces a Western-centric bias that hinders reflection of diverse cultural knowledge. The authors hypothesize models already hold rich cultural knowledge in local languages, with a mechanism to transfer it to weaker languages. On the BLEnD benchmark, their approach improves cultural alignment, boosting English query performance by an average of 5.03 percent using only their own data.
arxiv-2605-22237: Li, Wu and Miao rethink how neural networks run under fully homomorphic encryption, which allows only addition and multiplication. Instead of fitting high-degree polynomials to the ReLU activation, they seek a quadratic replacement that preserves the decisions of a trained single-layer network without retraining. Their geometric method gives exact conditions when possible and a relaxed version otherwise, and it runs faster than a high-degree rival in tests.
arxiv-2605-22337: Luo and colleagues present Meta-Soft, a method that compresses the key-value cache of large language models. Fixed soft-token methods use a static query, so they miss changing relevance. Evicted tokens are also lost for good, breaking context. Meta-Soft instead builds a library of learnable basis vectors. A selector then forms prompt-specific soft tokens from a sparse mix. Those tokens probe key information, and an attention-flow step folds dropped meaning into retained tokens. Tests show it beats rival eviction methods.
arxiv-2605-22437: Kučerák, Breier and Hou test the Intel Neural Compute Stick 2 under single-pulse electromagnetic fault injection. The device runs three ImageNet-trained convolutional networks on OpenVINO. Across about 17,500 trials, single pulses yield four outcomes: no change, minor silent corruption, major lasting degradation until reload, and hangs needing power-cycling. Major degradation strikes 18 to 31 percent of hotspot trials, with accuracy below five percent after collapse. Idle loaded devices can also be triggered, so load-time checks alone do not suffice.
arxiv-2605-22537: Blagoev and team propose Filtered Truncated Importance Sampling (F-TIS), a GRPO-style paradigm for heterogeneous models. In GRPO, completions are rewarded, and policy updates toward better ones. Generation is slow, and prior work spreads inference, assuming homogeneous models. Decentralized systems need heterogeneous models, but off-policy samples hurt convergence. F-TIS uses off-policy samples to improve local learning and cross-model collaboration. F-TIS matches on-sample final convergence, and sometimes beats on-policy training out-of-distribution by up to 12 percent.
arxiv-2605-22637: Kleger-Rudomin and others ask whether BioFET nanosensors, sensitive to tumour DNA in clean lab media, still detect it reliably in whole blood. Their simulation links operating point, screened charge transfer, finite binding, stray adsorption, background swings and electronic noise to a blank based threshold. Monte Carlo runs show short screening length and nanometre charge gaps weaken the current shift, while low frequency noise shrinks the gap to blank responses. Under the tested charge gating regime, simulated shifts fail to clear the threshold reliably at low tumour DNA levels.
arxiv-2605-23237: Cui, Qiao, and Jacobs introduce StereoGenBench, an Unreal benchmark for stereo generation. Stereo views need data where baseline, intrinsics, depth, and motion are known. Old sets give subsets of these variables, but common sets lack paired ground truth in one set source. Each scene uses a six-camera array, yielding up to 15 view pairs. Baselines run from narrow to wide, and every view ships with RGB, depth, settings, baselines, and poses. Splits include narrow and wide baseline sets. Dataset, test code, and generation code are public.
arxiv-2605-23437: Kovács improves the best construction of a line-free set in 3D space over a finite field, building on earlier joint work. His set reaches (p-1) cubed plus one eighth of p to the three-halves, up to linear error. That beats the plain hypercube construction by a superlinear extra term, the first such gain. By complementation, the same construction caps the smallest 2-blocking set in affine 3-space at 3p squared minus one eighth of p to the three-halves, up to linear error.
arxiv-2605-23537: Mateos and colleagues survey concomitant DAG learning, the task of inferring cause-effect maps from observed data alone. Classical methods struggle with the hard task of enforcing no cycles and with hidden confounding or uneven noise. The tutorial recasts structure learning as continuous scoring over link matrices, then covers methods that jointly infer sparse causal structure and noise levels, gaining robustness under uneven noise and distribution shifts. It closes with new directions in online, nonlinear, and neural causal discovery.
arxiv-2605-23737: Tang and Zhang give a spectral radius condition for a graph to contain k edge-disjoint 2-connected factors and spanning trees. The spectral radius of a graph is its adjacency matrix's eigenvalue, and a connected factor is a spanning subgraph. For a graph of order n with minimum degree at least 6 and n at least triple the minimum degree, the condition yields k edge-disjoint 2-connected factors. It yields floor of minimum degree minus 4k over 2 spanning trees, for k from 1 to floor of minimum degree over 4.
arxiv-2605-23837: Erez Sheiner settles a 52 year old question about Chomp, the chocolate bar game where a move eats a rectangle corner. Gale had computed that every three row board up to width 100 has exactly one winning first move and asked if that always holds. Sheiner proves it does for every width, using a two variable recurrence for losing positions. A rightmost hole principle splits the counting numbers into two move types, also naming the winning row, which is never the first.
arxiv-2605-24037: Zhou and seven co-authors turn motion forecasting into sequence models, lining up a set of modes so mode-to-mode links are explicit. ModeSeq decodes modes one by one, each built on earlier modes, spurring diverse guesses with trust order. Parallel ModeSeq keeps the same causal links with masked self-attention while decoding all modes at once, enabling large-K inference. With Early-Match-Take-All and a ranking regularizer, ModeSeq won the 2024 Waymo LiDAR-free motion track and Parallel ModeSeq won the 2025 Interaction Prediction Challenge.
arxiv-2605-24137: Nirujan and four co-authors study false claims in machine-written bug-report summaries, grading each part on its own. A first look at 80 structured summaries found nearly half missing facts and about an eighth inventing facts. From Mozilla bug reports, they plant controlled fake details to build a test set, then train a detector that flags tainted summaries and names the hit parts. The best model scores well on all three jobs, and common fault patterns show where summary tools still mislead developers.
arxiv-2605-24337: Weinberg and five co-authors explore cultural and linguistic identity in AI-generated voices for AAC. Voice marks identity, and for AAC users the device voice becomes their identity marker, yet finding a voice that fits linguistically and culturally is hard. A survey across eight countries finds transgender, non-binary, and non-US-born respondents rate current voice support lower than others. A tool eliciting cultural markers through guided questions generates voice candidates. Follow-up interviews show cultural alignment runs deeper than accent or language, touching belonging and self-recognition.
arxiv-2605-24437: Zhao and three co-authors present CAffNet, building hard constraint rules into feed networks and text models with input-set affine constraints of any size. Soft constraints give no rule promise, while post-fixing after training can yield weak results. The team adds a learned constraint-affine layer beyond fixed square or side maps, tuning jointly with network weights. The build sets no limits on constraint-space sizes, preserves full rule powers, and promises constraint keeping for every input. Tests across domains needing promised rules show robust scores.
arxiv-2605-24537: Iago N. Mamede and Francesco Coghi study rare trajectories of Markov processes through Doob fixed-time conditioning. The conditioning reshapes drift to guarantee a prescribed target at a time. Since the Doob drift rarely has a closed form, they view the conditioned ensemble as the process post-selected on the endpoint. That view yields an optimal-control formula for the leading term of the moment generating function, as a variational principle with terminal conditions from the Doob constraint. Two analytical examples and a heat-dissipation folding model illustrate the framework.
arxiv-2605-24737: Jehanne Dussert argues AI compliance should be a continuous runtime signal, not a binary audit-time verdict. The EU AI Act demands ongoing human oversight and drift detection in deployed systems. Her govllm framework routes model selection by compliance scores rather than latency or cost alone. A panel of regulatory judges, each specialized per criterion, turns disagreement into an uncertainty signal for arbitration. Tests on 49 pairs across five criteria show agreement topping out near 69 percent, with no model leading everywhere, and position bias costing up to 25 points.
arxiv-2605-24937: Iosif Lytras and Angelos Ntousis analyze schemes for stochastic differential equations with super-linear, locally Lipschitz drift, where the Euler-Maruyama method is unstable. They study the KL-accelerated tamed unadjusted Langevin algorithm and add a tamed randomized midpoint method. Two frameworks give non-asymptotic estimates: KL divergence for one scheme and total variation for the other. Under a logarithmic Sobolev inequality, the first scheme needs near-optimal epsilon to the minus one half KL iterations. The second gives a total variation guarantee under super-linear drift.
arxiv-2605-25237: Alexei Vazquez shows that the high shortest path multiplicity seen in real networks follows naturally from local evolution rules. Multiplicity counts how many distinct shortest paths join pairs of nodes, and it tracks community structure. For random graphs with any degree distribution, average multiplicity follows average k times k minus one over average k times e. It grows with network size when the degree exponent is at most three. Networks grown by stochastic local rules gain multiplicity faster than their randomized versions. Their community count grows alongside it.
arxiv-2605-25437: Fanhu Zeng and colleagues improve visual reasoning when several input sources, like infrared and depth, must be combined. Current methods treat extra sources as pure accumulation, missing whether fusion adds information or interference. Their MARS framework treats each modality as its own source and anchors advantage normalization on single-source rewards. That design rewards genuine information gain, encourages sources to promote each other, and suppresses noise and conflict. Tests show gains of 3.2 percent on one training method and 4.9 percent on another, across varied datasets.
arxiv-2605-25637: Hindov and Lokharu study sharp weighted Sobolev-type inequalities, which bound a weighted average of a function by the size of its higher derivative. They show every minimizer keeps one sign throughout, so it satisfies a nonlinear eigenvalue problem of polyharmonic type. That yields an explicit account of the extremizers across a broad class of weights. They also compute the optimal constant directly from the weight function. The estimates recover earlier sharp results and Hardy-type inequalities on finite intervals.
arxiv-2605-26037: Sun and Kazakov test reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards for knowledge-graph tool use, a deliberately tiny API of four Freebase moves. Training Qwen2.5-7B with GRPO lifts tool-grounded answers from 3.8 percent to 9.6 percent over 250 steps, then crashes them to zero within one 50-step window. That peak-then-collapse shape repeats across four seeds. Across seven reward designs, denser or sharper proxy rewards merely shift the failure mode. The authors blame thin interface feedback: an empty result list carries no hint, unlike a Python traceback naming the bad line.
arxiv-2605-26237: Cogolludo-Agustín and Măcinic introduce inequalities, called modular, for complements of plane curves, built from a combinatorial Aomoto complex tied to a curve's weak type. They use the tool to study twisted Alexander polynomials, especially the characteristic polynomial of the Milnor fiber of a projective plane curve. They give criteria for nontrivial resonance in degree one over positive-characteristic fields for quasi fiber-type curves, plus lower bounds for twisted root multiplicities. They apply the results to compute root multiplicities for fiber-type curves.
arxiv-2605-26537: Zhejian Zhou and Jonathan May hide messages in the reasoning style of chains of thought, not in word choice. A misaligned model might slip covert information past supervisors through encoded reasoning. Older schemes work at token or lexical level, where a paraphraser defends well. Conceptual steganography instead carries bits through high-level reasoning patterns per step. In tests spanning four model families and two reasoning domains, the channel survives strong paraphrase defense better than keyword methods, with utility intact. A strategy-aware paraphraser, however, closes much of the channel.
arxiv-2605-26637: Xueyang Zhou and nine others move robot skills out of one big policy and into callable tools. Unified policies struggle because perception, reasoning, planning, and control differ in kind and resist neat modular learning. Their Embodied Tool Protocol standardizes tool registration, discovery, calls, and runs. It draws on over 100 checked tools and a bench covering tool need, choice, use, and chaining. Tests show gains averaging 31 percent on one bench and 36 percent on another, strong for thought and sight but weak for action.
arxiv-2605-26837: In their 2026 paper, Jechumtál and ten colleagues test how interface roughness affects spin-current flow in cobalt-platinum stacks, using terahertz emission spectroscopy. Roughness is tuned via a gold buffer layer while other growth settings stay fixed. Surprisingly, spin-current transparency falls by only about 30 percent even as roughness and grain size triple, with no measurable change in the terahertz spectrum. Spin transport, they conclude, is robust to imperfect interfaces on ultrafast timescales.
arxiv-2605-26937: Giordano and Razniewski propose open knowledge evaluation, a new way to benchmark what language models actually state rather than what benchmark designers choose to ask. Instead of narrow preset questions, models answer open-ended prompts such as telling all they know about an entity. Their BeQu benchmark pairs 10,000 entities with reference corpora for statement verification. Tests across models probe how reasoning effort, scale, prompt format, and domain shape stated knowledge.
arxiv-2605-27237: Taehoon Kim, Sigrun Andradottir, Seong-Hee Kim, and Yuwei Zhou tackle deciding which simulated options meet probability limits. Their method uses yes-or-no simulation results directly instead of averaging them into batches. It also handles several thresholds per limit, stays statistically valid, and beats an older method built for normally distributed data.
arxiv-2605-27637: Krivoruchenko builds a spin-S projection for total and orbital angular momenta from the Frobenius covariant. It takes two forms: a polynomial in powers of the spin-orbital scalar product, and a finite sum over polarization terms. The result matches Villars' projection for angular momentum, used in studies of nuclear structure.
arxiv-2605-28137: Friedrich and colleagues isolate how unsafe training images drive unsafe image generation. Training identical models on datasets differing only in unsafe share, they find output unsafety climbs steadily with contamination, and the share, not the count, matters. Even at zero contamination a floor remains, traced partly to the frozen text encoder, while filtering costs no image quality.
arxiv-2605-28337: Gjergji and colleagues place facilities where some customer pairs must stay apart, as with hazards or rivals. Their wide-neighborhood hunt mixes three wrecking moves with an exact-fix repair step. On all open benchmarks it beat top rivals, setting fresh best answers on each case. The apart-customers variant fits real site problems that plain models miss.
arxiv-2605-28537: Jorik Jooken studies vertex-critical graphs avoiding a five-vertex path plus a chair or cricket graph as induced subgraphs. A graph is k-vertex-critical when it needs k colors but every proper induced subgraph needs fewer. He proves that for every k, only finitely many critical graphs exist for either forbidden pair. He characterizes all 5-critical graphs of both kinds and all 6-critical cricket graphs, bounding antichain sizes with Ramsey-type ideas. The results yield a fast test for (k-1)-colorability with a negative certificate on failure.
arxiv-2605-28637: Michael Sahre and four colleagues implement restricted open-shell Kohn-Sham density-functional for excited states in plane-wave VASP. Single-setup methods suffer spin contamination, but ROKS gives spin-pure singlet levels by tuning a mix of mixed-spin and triplet setups. The code, with atomic forces, matches Q-Chem on eight organic compounds to about 30 meV. For MgO with a neutral oxygen vacancy, ROKS excited-state levels track time-based density-functional theory closely while keeping ground-state scaling, giving cheap excited-state runs in large systems.
arxiv-2605-28737: Finn Larsen and Kartik Sharma construct smooth complex saddles for the supersymmetric index. Rather than the naive Euclidean continuation of the Lorentzian BPS hole, they build solutions for AdS3 times S3 black holes in the STU model. They reach the same BTZ times S3 geometries two ways: from two-center BPS solutions with complex dipole charges, and from six-dimensional black strings after imposing the BPS relation among conserved charges. Smoothness and periodicity conditions prove exactly those needed for globally well-defined supersymmetry and for the index's thermodynamic potentials.
arxiv-2605-29037: Victoria Bencheva and Velichka Milousheva study timelike meridian surfaces in 4D Minkowski space, a setting where time acts as a fourth part. They show all of them have flat normal connection, a strong shared trait that holds throughout the class. They sort the constant Gauss curvature cases, all minimal, and all non-zero constant mean curvature cases. No parallel mean curvature vector fields occur except constant-mean-curvature cases lying flat. They also cover cases with parallel scaled mean curvature vector field but non-parallel mean curvature vector.
arxiv-2605-29137: Daniel J. Spencer and colleagues offer a guide on quantum error correction and fault tolerance. Noise threatens qubits, and it must protect fragile states without copying them, checking them directly, or destroying their information. The guide builds codes, syndromes, stabilizers, and decoding, then connects them to code kinds and current research paths. Older and newer builds include topological, subsystem, bosonic, qudit, dynamic, and low-density parity-check codes. Focus falls on how each is used in design, checks, and fault-tolerant runs, for novices and experts alike.
arxiv-2605-29237: Junke Zhang presents MemoAttack, a black-box jailbreak framework built around a memory of attack skills that grows over time. Past attacks are boiled down to skill units pairing tactics with templates and evidence. That memory evolves through probation, promotion, retirement, reactivation, and cleanup. New attacks balance trusted reuse against trying new things when unsure. Across three target models, it beat the strongest baseline on each while cutting the cost of wins. As goals pile up, the effort needed per goal falls a lot.
arxiv-2605-29337: Amy Herron and Anne Thomas develop an app to show conjugation in affine Coxeter groups in 2D and 3D. Affine Coxeter groups are key objects in math and in crystallography, and conjugate group members share very similar algebraic and geometric traits. Using recent results of Milicevic, Schwer, and Thomas, the authors explain the math behind the visualization and connect it to the arts. The app makes an abstract algebraic pattern visible, linking group theory, geometry, and art.
arxiv-2605-29537: Eric Alsmann, Martin Lange, and Marco Sälzer map how hard it is to verify feedforward neural networks with quantized weights. They split exact-weight rational networks, quantized networks with finite-width math, and dynamic quantized networks run under given math. Two styles are used: linear programming constraints and bit-vector logic, which can express nonlinear constraints. With fixed width, checking stays NP-complete under both styles, matching the rational case. For dynamic quantization with bit-vector rules, upper bounds add to known PSPACE-hardness.
arxiv-2605-29637: Debajyoti Mazumder and five colleagues introduce IndicKLAR, covering 18 of 22 Indian languages, with speaker-verified code-mixed variants for 11 pairs. Across nine models, the native-to-English gap can reach about half, while code-mixed inputs shrink it to within five hundredths of English. Strategies exposing conversion explicitly were tested: translate-then-answer, joint translation-and-answer, and Translate-in-Thought, where models convert internally. A flip point, where predictions turn from incorrect to correct, appears between native and code-mixed settings, whether mixed input is given or produced internally.
arxiv-2605-29737: Alexander Sternfeld, Andrei Kucharavy, and Ljiljana Dolamic test whether tiny prompt tweaks can break the security of code from language models. They mutate prompts token by token across three models and five tongues, and find that even a one-letter change can flip output from safe to unsafe. Probes of hidden states show this brittleness is partly etched in prompt encodings, but patchily. Input-check flaws prove easier to foresee than flaws from one local unsafe choice, such as a weak algorithm.
arxiv-2605-30537: Yang, Zeng, and Yang ask whether picking training data for today's gains can hurt a language model tomorrow. Comparing six families of selection methods under one multi-stage protocol, they track not just immediate scores but later learning speed, forgetting, uneven skills, and robustness to unfamiliar data. Short-sighted picks often reverse rank: they lift the current stage while slowing later learning and deepening forgetting, a pattern the authors call myopic selection. They propose a long-horizon objective that weighs coverage and future transfer alongside immediate usefulness.
arxiv-2605-30837: Zhang and colleagues reframe prompt-injection defense as detector allocation. Prompt-injection detectors are heterogeneous, each strong on a different slice. Yet existing systems treat detection as a fixed pipeline. Their framework SCOUT predicts each detector's reliability and latency from similar past inputs. It exposes a safety-utility threshold to the operator. They build SCOUT-450, a benchmark of agent injections. On SCOUT-450, a safety point reduces attack rate by 46 percent and wall-clock by 40 percent relative to an always-on judge, at a 5.1-point benign drop.
arxiv-2605-31037: Lu, Jiang, and Huang establish a symmetry rule for spins robust to light polarization in antiferromagnets. Fast spin control has relied on circularly polarized lasers for spin, while robust forms have lacked a rule. Using density functional theory, they observe robust response in spin-spiral magnets and its loss in collinear magnets. Lasers induce loss, rotation, and wobble of spins in spin-spiral NiI2, while turning is largely lost in aligned magnets. The work reveals a pathway free of light type, opening fast spin control.
arxiv-2605-31537: Hai and team present a nonperturbative account of effective interactions in the fractional quantum Hall regime. It is built straight from the exact spectrum of two electrons in a magnetic field. Standard Haldane pseudopotentials project the Coulomb interaction onto lowest-Landau-level states, skipping virtual jumps to higher levels. Beyond that approximation, they define renormalized pseudopotentials from exact eigenenergies, with corrections staying negative and varying with strength and angular momentum.
arxiv-2606-00037:
Ferrario and Hatherley name a governance problem with deployed AI updates, in this 2026 arXiv paper. They call it update opacity: after a model update, users cannot see why the same input now gives a new output. Updates are needed to stop performance decaying, yet silent changes erode calibrated trust. The authors frame the issue as a failure of epistemic access over time: changes stop being clear to the people who must act on them.

Simply disclosing every change would swamp users, so relevance must be filtered. Their framework combines the European Union AI Act, which helps define which changes matter most, with MLOps tooling that tracks changes in practice. Systems would carry trustworthiness profiles, and threshold-based disclosure would surface only changes to each stakeholder group. A medical AI example shows the approach. The paper draws lessons for lifecycle documentation, post-market monitoring, and how update notices should be written.
arxiv-2606-00137:
Perla, Zhang, and Mahdavi-Amiri review how nets paint the skins of 3D mesh forms. A good skin makes a digital thing look real. New 3D tools can make shaped and skinned goods at once. Mesh forms still rule film, games, and design work, though.

The survey lays out the base ideas first. These span mesh shape, skin maps, and how nets dream up new skins. It sorts past work from GAN-based tools to fresh spread-based lines. It weighs net forms, teach styles, data sets, and test norms. It also notes shop-ready tools and open gaps. Readers get a clear map of where mesh skin work stands now.
arxiv-2606-00237:
Badurina and Zurek cast matter-wave tools as hunters for dark stuff. Such tools split a wave pack in two and let the halves drift apart. Dark stuff could leave a mark in phase or in lost sync. It need not drop much push or kick to do so.

The pair frame these marks in an open-field math built for such tools. A split shows in how the two marks scale with dark crowd counts. Phase grows at most in a straight line with counts. Lost sync can gain a boost or a block from crowd rules. The frame spans fast and slow dark moods. It also sorts fixes past the heavy-probe cap in a clean way.
arxiv-2606-00637:
Fu and co-authors split ground reads for humanoid walks into world and local watch strands. Reward-taught walks have leapt in skill of late. Sight-led plans still trip on thin step spots and tight rooms. Broad ground sense and fine step picks are both a must there.

Their frame, GLAD, splits those two jobs in a clean way. A world strand pools watch weight to sum the ground round the bot. A local strand thins traits by ground pull and state fit. That split keeps fine step cues from wash-out in the pool. Tests span gaps, step stones, and stairs in sim runs. Set acts spring up, like thin path trails and block dodges. A Unitree G1 bot runs the plan in real rooms by its own lidar.
arxiv-2606-00837:
Park and co-authors plan over long horizons with diffusion models in this 2026 paper. Diffusion models give strong priors for structured output. But many tasks need results far past the scale the models trained on. A common fix composes short local plans into one long output. Joined plans can agree with their neighbors yet form a poor whole.

Their method, CoFi, splits the work by scale at run time. First it aligns local drafts around a shared coarse scaffold. That scaffold holds the long-range shape of the route or task chain. CoFi then adds noise back to a mid level and denoises with the same local prior. Fine detail returns while the global shape holds. Older fixes repeat local passes or optimize at run time, which grows costly fast. Tests span long-horizon robot planning and more. The authors present CoFi as a cheaper path to coherent plans.
arxiv-2606-01037:
Fernando and Kousik study a family of polynomials over finite fields in this 2026 maths paper. The polynomial g, indexed by n and a prime power q, was built to find new classes of permutation polynomials. A permutation polynomial shuffles the field's elements with no repeats. Such shuffles serve codes, ciphers, and designs.

The pair study how g permutes fields of even characteristic. They lift the polynomial to many variables and sort the permutation behavior there. Local permutation polynomials that stem from g get the same care. New identities for g are proved along the way. Open questions on when g permutes close the paper. The work suits algebraists who mine one seed polynomial for whole families of shuffles. Each identity trims the search for the next class.
arxiv-2606-01137:
Ercole links digital maturity to hospital efficiency in England in this 2026 paper. Whether digital health spending lifts hospital productivity is a live policy question. Past evidence is mixed, and causal claims are hard to pin down. He studies NHS acute trusts, the big hospital groups of the English health service, with a Bayesian stochastic frontier model.

The model fits a four input production function to 111 acute non specialist trusts for 2024/25. Inputs come from audited NHS accounts, from clinical staff to capital. A digital maturity score enters the inefficiency side, with controls for deprivation, teaching status, and finances. Higher maturity goes with lower inefficiency, at high posterior confidence. Top quartile trusts operate at 98.0 percent of their production frontier in the estimates. The bottom quartile sits at 93.2 percent for the lowest quartile in the same model. The gap is worth about 20 million pounds per trust, he estimates.
arxiv-2606-01237:
Shen and co-authors build a tool to spot early cognitive decline. Mild impairment and felt decline sit on the Alzheimer's path. Clear, open diagnosis helps early risk checks and care. Brain network models can sort cases well. But they show little about which links change. The GCAN tool frames the task as a what-if swap. It makes target-state networks from source-state inputs. Gaps between them form attention maps that guide the call.

An atlas-aware transformer keeps the network shape intact. The tool joins function and structure links in one model. Tests use clinic data and the ADNI dataset. Tasks split healthy, felt-decline, and impaired groups. GCAN scores well and gives views that aid trust.
arxiv-2606-01537:
Liu, Maeda, and Pancholy teach chest X-ray models from body signals. Diagnosis often joins imaging with physiological measurements. Deployed models usually work on one data type alone. PaCX-MAE injects physiological priors into X-ray encoders. It stays strictly unimodal when used at inference time. Masked autoencoding in-domain forms the base training. A dual contrastive-predictive objective aligns X-ray features with paired signals. ECG and lab embeddings supply those paired signals.

Nine benchmarks show consistent gains over domain-specific MAE. Physiology-dependent tasks gain most from the method. Label efficiency is high in the 1 percent regime. Segmentation parity with MAE holds at the same time. Attention checks show focus on signs like the cardiac silhouette.
arxiv-2606-01637:
Qu, Fu, and Hu test whether peer pressure misleads language models. Models in multi-agent systems see and answer other agents' replies. Conformity is a key risk in that setup. A model may drop its own answer just because others agree elsewhere. Past work shows models often revise toward a majority answer. Whether revisions fix errors as often as they cause them was unclear. Their controlled study gives a model a question first. Simulated peer responses then appear before its final decision.

Two social cues get varied: consensus structure and authority labels. Four open-weight models and seven QA datasets take part. Peer agreement misleads correct models far more easily than it corrects wrong ones. Authority labels raise uptake of the endorsed answer, right or wrong. Chain-of-thought and reflection do not reliably cut harmful revision.
arxiv-2606-01737:
Li and co-authors assign traffic accident liability with a multimodal RAG system. Liability analysis matters for transport systems and legal aid. Past methods suffer low efficiency and subjective judgment. Results can be inconsistent across analysts as well. LLMs are limited by noisy video inputs and thin legal knowledge. TrafficRAG first turns accident scenes into structured text descriptions. A vision-language model produces those descriptions as retrieval queries. Hybrid retrieval joins BM25 with dense embedding search. It fetches traffic regulations and similar historical cases.

The model then reasons over legal knowledge and accident evidence together. Standardized, legally grounded liability reports come out at the end. Legal Norm Adaptation Accuracy reaches 77 point 32 percent. Factual Faithfulness reaches 81 point 71 percent in their tests.
arxiv-2606-02137:
Zengin and Köroğlu build quantum codes from cyclic codes over a composite ring. The ring mixes the field F2 with a second component. That component is F2 plus v times F2, with v squared equal to v. Cyclic codes over this ring are the starting point. Generator polynomials for their Hermitian hulls are determined.

Hermitian sums of the codes are also characterized. Quantum error-correcting codes follow from these structures. The Hermitian dual form of Quantum Construction X is applied. It acts on the hulls and sums obtained. Entanglement-assisted codes come from a second route. Matrix product methods act on LCD codes over the ring. Families of both code types are derived. Quantum coding theory gains new explicit families.
arxiv-2606-02337:
Amaya-Corredor and co-authors study teams of agents that must act together under limits. Two problems make this hard. The joint action space grows fast as agents are added. Added rules also link agents in ways that rewards alone miss. Their framework, CG-CMARL, joins coordination graphs with Lagrangian duality.

The system splits the joint task into pairs of agents. Shared value functions score the main goal and each constraint. At run time, message passing settles the joint action. A single multiplier sets the balance between goal and limits. One trained model can thus trace a full Pareto front. The authors prove convergence under mild terms.
